name: Amara Okafor
blurb: First-year physics PhD student taking graduate quantum and statistical mechanics.

uncertainty-disturbance.text: thinks the uncertainty principle comes from the measurement disturbing the particle

entropy-disorder.text: treats entropy as visual disorder rather than the log of the number of microstates

energy-kt-always.text: thinks the average energy is kT for any system at any temperature

sessions.title: What does a wavefunction tell you?

checks.q: What is $|3 + 4i|^2$?
What is $\frac{d}{dx} e^{ikx}$?
checks.k: $ik\,e^{ikx}$

checks.q: What does $|\psi(x)|^2\,dx$ give?
o: The probability of finding the particle between x and x + dx
checks.k: The probability of finding the particle between x and x + dx
checks.a: The probability of finding the particle between x and x + dx

checks.q: $\psi = (|0\rangle + i|1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$. Probability of measuring 1?
$\psi(x) = A$ on $[0, 4]$, zero elsewhere. What is A?
What is $[\hat x, \hat p]$?
checks.k: $i\hbar$

checks.q: Two observables commute. What does that allow?
o: A shared set of eigenstates, so both have definite values together
checks.k: A shared set of eigenstates, so both have definite values together
checks.a: A shared set of eigenstates, so both have definite values together

checks.q: Where does $\Delta x\,\Delta p \ge \hbar/2$ come from?
o: The state itself: x and p don't commute, so no state is sharp in both
The measuring photon kicks the particle
checks.k: The state itself: x and p don't commute, so no state is sharp in both
checks.a: The measuring photon kicks the particle

checks.q: An electron is confined to $\Delta x = 1$ nm. Minimum $\Delta p$ in units of $\hbar$ / nm?
A Gaussian wavepacket is made narrower in x. What happens to its momentum spread, and why?
checks.k: It grows, because a narrower packet needs more plane-wave components (Fourier width)
checks.a: It grows because measuring position more precisely disturbs it more

sessions.title: The harmonic oscillator with ladder operators

checks.q: Energy levels of the quantum harmonic oscillator?
checks.k: $\hbar\omega(n + 1/2)$

checks.q: What does $\hat a$ do to $|n\rangle$?
checks.k: $\sqrt{n}\,|n-1\rangle$

checks.q: What is $[\hat a, \hat a^\dagger]$?
Why must the ladder stop at a ground state?
checks.k: Energy is bounded below, so lowering must eventually give a|0> = 0
checks.a: Because energy can't be negative, a|0> has to vanish

checks.q: A diatomic molecule's vibration at room temperature is mostly in which state?
o: The ground state, since ħω is much larger than kT
checks.k: The ground state, since ħω is much larger than kT

checks.q: How many outcomes does measuring $S_z$ on a spin-½ give?
Spin up along z, measured along x. Probability of +ħ/2?
First-order energy shift from a perturbation V?
o: $\langle n | V | m \rangle$ summed over m
checks.k: $\langle n | V | n \rangle$

checks.q: Why does second-order theory push the ground state down?
checks.k: Every term has a negative denominator E_0 - E_m, so each contribution lowers the energy

checks.q: Why can't a spin be sharp along both x and z at once?
o: $S_x$ and $S_z$ don't commute, so no state is an eigenstate of both
It can, with a careful measurement
checks.k: $S_x$ and $S_z$ don't commute, so no state is an eigenstate of both

sessions.title: The Boltzmann distribution and partition functions

checks.q: Probability of a state with energy E at temperature T is proportional to...
Two levels at 0 and ε with $\varepsilon = kT \ln 3$. What is Z?
How do you get ⟨E⟩ from Z?
checks.k: $-\partial \ln Z / \partial \beta$

checks.q: When does each quadratic degree of freedom carry kT/2?
o: When kT is large compared with the level spacing
checks.k: When kT is large compared with the level spacing
checks.a: When kT is large compared with the level spacing

checks.q: A 3D classical ideal gas: ⟨E⟩ per atom in units of kT?
Boltzmann's entropy formula?
checks.k: $S = k \ln \Omega$

checks.q: Oil and water separate on their own. Did total entropy fall?
o: No; hydrogen bonding of water raises the entropy of the whole system
Yes, the mixture became more ordered
checks.k: No; hydrogen bonding of water raises the entropy of the whole system
checks.a: Yes, the mixture became more ordered

checks.q: Helmholtz free energy in terms of Z?
checks.k: $F = -kT \ln Z$

checks.q: At fixed T and V, why does a system minimise F rather than E?
checks.k: Minimising F = E - TS maximises the total entropy of system plus reservoir
checks.a: Because entropy also matters at finite T

checks.q: Ω goes from $10^{20}$ to $10^{21}$. What is ΔS in units of k (to 2 decimals)?

sessions.title: Fermions, bosons and the quantum statistics

checks.q: Fermi–Dirac occupation of a level at E = μ?
Why does the Fermi–Dirac occupation never exceed 1?
o: Pauli exclusion: at most one fermion per state
checks.k: Pauli exclusion: at most one fermion per state
checks.a: Pauli exclusion: at most one fermion per state

checks.q: What happens to Bose–Einstein occupation as E − μ → 0⁺?
o: It diverges, the start of condensation
checks.k: It diverges, the start of condensation

checks.q: Why do metal electrons add almost nothing to heat capacity at room temperature?
o: Only electrons within about kT of the Fermi level can be excited
checks.k: Only electrons within about kT of the Fermi level can be excited

checks.q: Why does a solid's heat capacity drop below 3Nk at low temperature?
o: Vibrational modes freeze out when kT falls below ħω
checks.k: Vibrational modes freeze out when kT falls below ħω
checks.a: Vibrational modes freeze out when kT falls below ħω

links.why: Used the squared modulus of a complex amplitude to get a probability.
Got the minimum momentum spread from the x–p commutator bound.
Now limits equipartition to kT above the level spacing, after giving a stiff vibration kT earlier.
Summed Boltzmann factors to get the two-level Z.
Explained free-energy minimisation through total entropy.
Gave every electron 3kT/2, as equipartition would, instead of Fermi–Dirac occupation.
